blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — foundational multidrug therapy for HFrEF
stem: A client has symptomatic chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Assuming no contraindications and that each drug is clinically appropriate, which regimen contains one agent from each of the four foundational medication classes recommended in current HFrEF therapy?

options.A: Sacubitril/valsartan, metoprolol succinate extended-release, spironolactone, and dapagliflozin provide ARNI, evidence-based beta-blocker, MRA, and SGLT2-inhibitor therapy.
options.B: Sacubitril/valsartan, furosemide, digoxin, and amlodipine provide an ARNI plus symptomatic or adjunctive agents but omit several foundational HFrEF drug classes.
options.C: Lisinopril, losartan, sacubitril/valsartan, and aliskiren concentrate therapy within the renin-angiotensin system rather than representing four distinct foundational classes.
options.D: Metoprolol tartrate, diltiazem, furosemide, and aspirin include cardiovascular drugs but do not supply the four recommended foundational HFrEF medication classes.

rationale: Current 2026 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic guidance states that four medication classes are recommended as core therapy for HFrEF: renin-angiotensin system inhibition with an ARNI, ACE inhibitor, or ARB; an evidence-based beta blocker; a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; and an SGLT2 inhibitor. The 2024 ACC HFrEF Expert Consensus likewise identifies ARNI, evidence-based beta blocker, MRA, and SGLT inhibitor as core GDMT and recommends early initiation when feasible. Option A provides one appropriate representative from each class: sacubitril/valsartan, metoprolol succinate extended-release, spironolactone, and dapagliflozin. The other regimens omit core classes or duplicate renin-angiotensin pathway therapy.
educational_objective: Identify the four foundational HFrEF medication classes and recognize a regimen containing one appropriate representative from each: RAS inhibition, evidence-based beta blocker, MRA, and SGLT2 inhibitor.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology; American College of Cardiology
source_document_title: 2026 AHA/ACC/ADA/ASN Guideline for Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome; 2024 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway for Treatment of HFrEF
source_version_date: 2026 CKM guideline published 2026; 2024 ACC HFrEF consensus current and accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: 2026 CKM guideline §6.3.1: for HFrEF, four medication classes are recommended as core therapy — RASi (ARNI, ACEi, or ARB), beta blockers, MRA, and SGLT2i. 2024 ACC HFrEF Expert Consensus Key Point 1: core GDMT includes an ARNI, evidence-based beta blocker, SGLT inhibitor, and MRA, with early rapid initiation when feasible.
source_claim_supported: Contemporary guidance continues to identify four core HFrEF medication classes: RAS inhibition, evidence-based beta blocker, MRA, and SGLT2 inhibitor.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate medication appropriateness, understand expected actions/outcomes, educate clients, and safely manage prescribed therapies.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote every choice as a full four-drug regimen interpretation of comparable length.
Removed the original uniquely-long key cue while preserving one representative from each current foundational class.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely supplies all four contemporary core HFrEF classes. Option lengths are closely matched and no second regimen is defensible as four-class foundational GDMT.
